packages.prose_explanation: The method extracts first-hop interaction sequences for source and destination nodes, padding them to a uniform length. These sequences are then stacked along a specific dimension to create a unified tensor representation that aligns heterogeneous features.

formula_obligations.mathematical_goal: Extract the first-hop interaction sequence of a node and encode it using node, edge, absolute temporal, and co-occurrence signals. Pass the aligned encoding through a continuous SSM that has been redesigned to make forgetting depend on the elapsed timespan and to selectively attend to important past inputs. Redefine the SSM step size Δt as a learnable, monotonically increasing function of the time gap, inspired by Ebbinghaus’ forgetting curve. Initialize the state transition matrix A as a diagonal matrix with negative real-part eigenvalues to guarantee stable exponential decay with increasing timespan. Redefine B and C as input-dependent matrices with spectral norm constraints, allowing the model to review important historical interactions while suppressing noise. For link prediction, use two independent DyG-Mamba encoders for source and destination nodes, pool their outputs, concatenate, and apply an MLP predictor; for node classification, use a single encoder without co-occurrence encoding.
exact_source_quotes: Extract the first-hop interaction sequence of a node and encode it using node, edge, absolute temporal, and co-occurrence signals.

packages.latex: \Delta t = f_{\text{time}}(\tau), \quad A = A_0, \quad B = B_{\text{spec}}, \quad C = C_{\text{spec}}
packages.prose_explanation: This package formalizes the author's intent to make the SSM's forgetting mechanism temporally aware. By linking $\Delta t$ to the timespan $\tau$, the model can forget older states more aggressively. The stable initialization of $A$ ensures that the system does not diverge, while the spectral norm constraints on $B$ and $C$ provide a robust mechanism for selective attention to historical data.

packages.latex: \begin{aligned} \Delta t_i &= \sigma\left( w_{\Delta t} \cdot \phi(\tau_i) \right), \quad \tau_i = t_{\text{pred}} - t_i \\ A &= \text{diag}(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n), \quad \text{Re}(\lambda_j) < 0 \forall j \\ B_i &= \frac{B_i^{\text{raw}}}{\|B_i^{\text{raw}}\|_2}, \quad C_i = \frac{C_i^{\text{raw}}}{\|C_i^{\text{raw}}\|_2} \end{aligned}
packages.prose_explanation: This package formalizes the author's intent to decouple the SSM's forgetting mechanism from the input sequence length by tying $\Delta t$ to the absolute timespan $\tau_i$. The diagonal initialization of $A$ with negative real parts ensures that the state $h_i$ decays exponentially over time, with the decay rate modulated by $\Delta t_i$. The spectral norm redefinition of $B$ and $C$ acts as a robustness constraint, ensuring that the selective mechanism (which determines how much of the input is written to the state and how much of the state is read out) is invariant to the scale of the projected features, thereby enabling stable and robust selective reviewing.
